subject: Request: Compensatory allowance for delayed multi-model rollout
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@brighthealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Compensatory allowance for delayed multi-model rollout

Susan —

Quick note following our sync this morning. We had planned to have multi-model routing (alpha) available for BrightHealth’s pilot by July 1st so the integration could run against the targeted ensemble in time for your internal validation window. The runtime team has hit a blocker with the quantized KV cache behavior when mixing model families; delivery is slipping ~4–6 weeks.

I know this derails your go-live timeline for the pilot features that depend on heterogeneous ensembles. Procurement asked whether we can provide a commercial accommodation tied to the delay while we remediate: specifically a one-off usage allowance or percentage rebate until the multi-model path is in production.

Attached: MA-terms-v2.pdf (proposed legal wording stub) and integration-plan.xlsx (high level rollout timeline).

Proposed customer-facing options to consider (I can formalize numbers if you want):
- Option A: One-time token allowance equal to 50M inference tokens (covers your expected pilot consumption through the delayed window)
- Option B: 10% invoice credit applied over next 3 billing cycles (protects BrightHealth on unit economics while we ship)

As discussed, we want to be pragmatic: keep the pilot live, avoid procurement churn, and retain the expansion motion. I’m looping in Laura and Mina to align on commercial / product conditionality and Jonas/Marcus for exec visibility if needed.

Next step: Susan — can you confirm which approach procurement prefers (tokens vs. credit) and whether they need a DocuSign-ready clause? I’ll put a short internal recommendation together with concrete dollar/token numbers.

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

Attachments: MA-terms-v2.pdf (attachment), integration-plan.xlsx (attachment)

From: Susan Park <susan.park@brighthealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brighthealth.com
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 14:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Compensatory allowance for delayed multi-model rollout

Karthik —

Thanks for the transparency and the options. Procurement will prefer a credit applied to invoices (less internal tracking), but I need a formal proposal with the estimated dollar impact and the exact time window. We cannot sign open-ended allowances without a cap or expiration.

A couple quick asks from procurement:
- A short clause we can attach to the Master Agreement (DocuSign preferred) that states the credit amount, trigger (delivery milestone), and expiry.
- The cap in USD or tokens and the redemption timeline (e.g., applied over next N invoices).

I’m cc’ing procurement to keep them in the loop. If you can get me a recommended option + numbers by EOD Friday we’ll review and push internally.

Appreciate it —
Susan Park
Program Lead, Strategic Integrations
BrightHealth
susan.park@brighthealth.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: Compensatory allowance for delayed multi-model rollout

Team —

Forwarding BrightHealth’s ask. Summary and recommendation below; please weigh in with approvals or alternate numbers.

Summary of impact:
- Pilot ARR opportunity: ~$180k ARR (expected first 6 months of usage)
- Immediate risk: pilot delay threatens qualification for expansion budget this quarter

Commercial recommendation (clean, limited scope):
- Recommendation: Apply a provisional one-time concession that minimizes bookkeeping and preserves our unit economics.
  - Proposal: 12% invoice credit applied pro rata across the next 2 billing cycles, capped at $45,000 total.
  - Conditions: Credit triggered only if multi-model routing is not available by 2028-08-01; credit expires if feature ships before this date.
  - Legal: Add a narrowly scoped amendment to MA-terms-v2.pdf specifying cap, trigger, and expiration. DocuSign link will be used to capture signature.

Rationale: keeps the pilot intact, reduces procurement friction, and limits our financial exposure. Token allowances are operationally clunkier for procurement and add reconciliation work.

Requested approvals / asks:
1) Jonas — executive sign-off on the $45k cap and 12%/$ amount
2) Marcus/Finance — confirm we can process a one-off credit memo and that the cap is under your review threshold
3) Karthik — prepare the DocuSign clause and final proposal for Susan by EOD Friday

I’ve attached the integration-plan.xlsx with the revised target milestones.

Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: integration-plan.xlsx (attachment)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 Jul 2028 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Compensatory allowance for delayed multi-model rollout

Laura / team —

I’ve reviewed and I approve the proposed conservative path. Confirming executive sign-off for the following:

- Approve: 12% invoice credit applied pro rata over the next 2 invoices, capped at $45,000 (DEAL-8421).
- Contingency: Credit is conditional on the remediation timeline and requires updated SLA language that the product team will provide; if the feature ships before 2028-08-01 the credit will not apply.
- Operations: Finance (Marcus) to generate a one-off credit memo; Sales Ops (Laura) to prepare DocuSign amendment referencing MA-terms-v2.pdf.

Karthik — run the updated clause by Susan and procurement. Once BrightHealth acknowledges acceptance, Marcus/Finance and Legal can finalize the paperwork.

Nice work turning this into a simple, capped accommodation. Please keep this thread for audit trail.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
VP, Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
